text:
Ashley Chen: Heads up — found a coupling in the operator claim merge logic that causes duplicate intents for long-lived jobs. noticed while debugging a tenant isolation test.
Mohit Patel: hmm, duplicate intents how? is it at mint time or at runtime aggregation?
Ashley Chen: runtime aggregation. when operator proxy stitches service claims + project claims we sometimes emit two 'write:models' intents if both parent and child scopes map to the same role.
Jamie K: ah yeah that can blow up the authz cache churn. any repro?
Ashley Chen: small one: background model-writer job calls via operator proxy, operator attaches operator:job claim and proxy also forwards svc-project:write. downstream RBAC layer treats them as separate grants.
Elaine Gomez: consequence? overpermissive? or just dup counting?
Ashley Chen: mainly duplicate audit log entries and inflated role graphs causing the permission scan to run twice. in worst case it can hit the 50k actor edge and slow checks.
Mohit Patel: we could canonicalize claims into a set and dedupe by (resource, action) tuple before RBAC expansion. cheap?
Jamie K: cheap in concept, but careful: some claims have qualifiers (env=prod) that change semantics. dedupe only safe for identical qualifiers.
Elaine Gomez: What about coalescing at the proxy with a precedence rule: operator claims override project-level claims and we drop duplicates?
Ashley Chen: that helps but then we risk hiding legitimate separate actor intents coming from different attestation chains. also affects telemetry attribution.
Mohit Patel: proposal: add an "origin" tag to expanded grants and dedupe only when origin equivalence holds OR when we can prove origin is functionally equivalent. fallback to keeping both when uncertain.
Jamie K: that sounds like more metadata plumbing across the authz pipeline. do we have capacity?
Elaine Gomez: it's reasonable — we already tag tokens with issuer id. extend to include chain-hash and reason. then RBAC expansion can check chain-hash equality before merging.
Ashley Chen: example quick patch (pseudo):
```
claims = normalize(claims)
expanded = []
for c in claims:
  grants = expand(c)
  for g in grants:
    key = (g.resource, g.action, c.chain_hash)
    if key not in seen: seen.add(key); expanded.append(g)
```
Mohit Patel: chain_hash idea good. we should also add a TTL for chain-hash caching to avoid unbounded growth.
Jamie K: agree. also we should add unit test asserting audit lines dedupe for same chain vs keep for different chain.
Elaine Gomez: one more edge: what about service-to-service proxies where the chain gets rewritten (operator inserts new link)? chain_hash will differ but semantics same. need a canonicalization step that strips intermediary proxy hops when evaluating equivalence.
Ashley Chen: we can canonicalize by keeping only attestations that assert effective actor and scope, drop transit-only hops. will need careful spec.
Mohit Patel: ops impact: this reduces audit noise and RBAC blowups, but could mask a misconfigured operator if we over-canonicalize. include an opt-in flag on proxies to preserve raw chain for debug.
Jamie K: sounds like action items: 1) spec chain-hash + canonicalization rules 2) implement dedupe in proxy + RBAC expansion 3) add TTL and opt-in raw-chain flag 4) tests + perf benchmark.
Elaine Gomez: +1. I'll own the spec doc. Ashley/Mohit you two pair on the prototype? Jamie can help with tests.
Ashley Chen: I can start a PR for prototype this week. will include a perf microbenchmark showing reduction in RBAC expansions.
Mohit Patel: I'll add chain-hash generator and TTL cache in authn service.
Jamie K: I'll write the test harness and audit assertions.
sec-bot: Reminder: please include security review label on PR and run staging authz smoke before merging. :lock:
Ashley Chen: noted. tagging sec-review. thanks all.
